composio.note: Composio provides a managed Todoist OAuth app, which works for prototypes. A separate Todoist MCP toolkit exists and needs your own app.

need_own_app.answer: Not for prototypes, because Composio provides a managed Todoist app. For production you will usually want your own app so users see your brand and you get your own quota.
reasons: Users see your app name instead of Composio on the consent screen
Managed apps share quota across all Composio users; your own app gets a dedicated quota
Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval; your own app can use shorter ones where supported

prerequisites.title: Todoist account
prerequisites.detail: The developer platform is free with any Todoist account. A Pro account may be needed for development, and Todoist can help if you lack one.

prerequisites.title: Verified Todoist user account
prerequisites.detail: Needed before you can submit for certification.

prerequisites.title: Listing assets and policies
prerequisites.detail: Prepare a marketing description, installation instructions, website and privacy policy links, a 250x250 JPG icon and 1600x1000 JPG screenshots. All links must use HTTPS and the privacy policy must not allow selling or sharing user data without consent.

steps.title: Prototype with Composio's managed Todoist app
steps.detail: Create the connection with the managed Todoist toolkit to test your agent before registering your own app.
steps.done_when: A test user can connect Todoist through Composio.

steps.title: Create your app in App Management Console
steps.detail: Register the app and note the Client ID and Client Secret it is assigned.
steps.done_when: You have a Client ID and Client Secret.

steps.title: Check Composio redirect URI
steps.detail: Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard and confirm it is HTTPS. If you set several redirect URIs, requests must pass redirect_uri.
steps.done_when: The URI is ready to paste.

steps.title: Add redirect URI in the console
steps.detail: Paste the Composio redirect URI into the app's OAuth2 redirect URLs.
steps.done_when: The redirect URL is saved in the console.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create a Todoist auth config through Composio's API with your own Client ID and Secret, and request only the scopes you need.
steps.done_when: The auth config exists and a test connection succeeds.

steps.title: Test with a real user account
steps.detail: Connect a second Todoist account and confirm the consent screen shows your app name.
steps.done_when: The connected account can run tool calls.

steps.title: Draft listing text and prepare assets
steps.detail: Write the description with the required non-affiliation statement, an 'x for Todoist' style name, and check images against the size and theme rules.
steps.done_when: All form fields are ready in English.

steps.title: Record demo and submit the form
steps.detail: Record a demo video showing the integration working, then submit the app submissions form.

steps.title: Wait for Todoist review
steps.detail: Todoist aims to respond within ten business days. Reply to follow-up emails, which Todoist aims to answer within two business days.
steps.done_when: Todoist publishes your listing and gives a public link.

traps.title: Dynamically registered client secrets do not expire
traps.detail: Dynamically registered client secrets do not expire.

traps.title: Maximum token limit on authorizations
traps.detail: If your app exceeds the maximum token limit, users get an invalid_application_status error when they authorize. The number of tokens allowed was not found.

traps.title: Naming and branding rules
traps.detail: Todoist cannot be the primary app name; use a form like 'x for Todoist' and state the app is not created by or affiliated with Todoist.

traps.title: Listing excludes automation-only integrations
traps.detail: Services that integrate only through IFTTT, Zapier or email forwarding are not listed. The app must complement Todoist, not copy its features.

traps.title: Review rejects broken apps
traps.detail: The app must be free of functional errors during Todoist's testing, and native apps must be signed with a trusted certificate.

traps.title: Webhook URL rules
traps.detail: Webhook URLs must use HTTPS with no port. A user's webhook activates only after that user completes your app's OAuth flow.

traps.title: Apps can be suspended
traps.detail: Todoist may suspend an application for abuse.

blockers.what_it_means: Your app hit the maximum token limit or was suspended for abuse.
blockers.what_to_do: Contact Todoist developer support and ask about the token limit and certification.

blockers.what_it_means: One of the submission, technical or marketing reviews found a problem.
blockers.what_to_do: Fix the listed issues and reply by email.
blockers.agent_can_help: Revise listing text and check image sizes against the rules.
